recentItems.title: Education dept. threatens legal action against parents for school shutdown  over poor conditions
recentItems.description:
Parents of learners at Khulanolwazi Primary School in Braamfischer, Soweto have closed the school in protest against what they term is the poor state of the school.

They've accused the Gauteng Department of Education of failure to intervene, despite repeated pleas for help.

As a result, their children have not been to school for three weeks.

The Department has threatened legal action against the parents.

recentItems.title: NCRS warns against sale of illicit products
recentItems.description:
Traders selling non-compliant, illicit and unsafe goods will face heavy prosecution and possible suspension from trading anywhere in South Africa. 

This follows a series of sting operations on informal and formal traders in the North West, conducted by the National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications.

The aim is to seize and remove unsafe goods and hold non-compliant traders accountable.

recentItems.title: New York Mayor releases records on toxic air ahead of 9/11 Anniversary
recentItems.description:
Ahead of the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, New York City has released more than 170 000 pages of previously withheld records that could shed new light on what officials knew about the toxic air around Ground Zero days after the attack. 

The documents point to concerns inside government about asbestos, other contaminants and potential legal liability, even as the public was being reassured about air safety. 

Mayor Zohran Mamdani says this is only the first release — ending a years-long legal battle over records that survivors and first responders have sought for decades.

recentItems.title: SA exploring opportunities in its creative economy
recentItems.description:
The Director General of the World Intellectual Property Organization Daren Tang says he will continue to promote cooperation and collaboration, despite a number of challenges facing the world.

Speaking to SABC News in Johannesburg, he says the world shouldn't be intimidated by the advent of artificial intelligence.

Dang also used his visit to the country to engage with government officials.

Khayelihle Khumalo has more.

recentItems.title: Public Works to brief media at Telkom Towers
recentItems.description:
In a statement, Public Works says that for more than a decade, the Telkom Towers have become a source of wasteful spending, leaving the property vacant while costing taxpayers millions of rand in maintenance and security. Today marks the beginning of significant steps towards revitalising the precinct and ensuring it delivers value for the public.

The Minister of Public Works and Infrastructure, Dean Macpherson, is expected to brief the media on an important announcement regarding the future of the expected R2.2 billion redevelopment of the Telkom Towers Precinct.

After much struggling, these gates were finally opened…
The gate has not been opened in a while, has rusted and is stuck.

Lennox Mabaso from Public Works explains why one of the gates that officials struggled to open ahead of the media briefing at the Telkom Towers in Pretoria was closed.
